items.title: metpo-proposal: route reused-ontology CURIEs to mappings, not definition_source
items.body:
The `metpo-proposal` skill (`.claude/skills/metpo-proposal/SKILL.md`) lists, under acceptable `definition_source` (IAO:0000119) forms:

> Reused PATO/GO definition → the source CURIE itself → `PATO:0000052`

`definition_source` means "where the definition text came from" (PMID, DOI, BacDive, ISBN). A reused ontology term is a **cross-ontology mapping**, not provenance. Emitting those CURIEs into `definition_source` conflates the two: no exact/close/narrow distinction, no mapping justification or confidence, and invisible to SSSOM tooling. This is the same conflation tracked in berkeleybop/metpo#344 (124 such rows already in the METPO sheet).

Proposal: when a proposed term reuses or aligns to an existing ontology class, emit it as a mapping annotation with an IRI (`skos:exactMatch` / `skos:closeMatch` / `skos:narrowMatch`, or `oboInOwl:hasDbXref`) in a dedicated column, and reserve `definition_source` for real citations. Update the SKILL guidance and `scripts/extract_metpo_proposals.py` accordingly.

Cross-repo cleanup hub: berkeleybop/metpo#344.

items.title: The upstream re-sync imports four grounding regressions and net-increases name ambiguity 572 -> 634
items.body:
Found by adversarial review of #786 and verified independently.

The re-sync in #786 pulls `mappings/culturebotai_reviewed_ingredients.tsv` and `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` from `../MediaIngredientMech` at `5530527b`. It fixes Cobalamine, but brings in regressions.

**Live in the shipped SSSOM** (name -> CURIE resolution changes):

| name | master | after sync |
|---|---|---|
| `alpha-Lactose` | CHEBI:36219 alpha-lactose | **CHEBI:189432 Alpha-lactose monohydrate** |
| `Carboxymethyl cellulose` | CHEBI:85146 carboxymethylcellulose | **CHEBI:234035 carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt** |

Both arrive as `skos:exactMatch` on the `MIM:` subject — an anhydrous/hydrate and a free-acid/sodium-salt false identity, exactly what the `hydrate_equivalences` closeMatch machinery exists to prevent. The other new MIM rows use closeMatch correctly, so this looks like a slip rather than a policy change. Also wrong in the file though not yet moving resolution: `MIM:Berberine` -> `CHEBI:31271 "Berberine chloride (TN)"` exactMatch, and `MIM:36-Dihydroxyflavone` -> `CHEBI:24698 hydroxyflavone` (a class) with its CAS dropped.

**Latent in the vendored TSV** (held back only because the additive baseline still holds the correct record — verified in `mappings/culturebotai_reviewed_ingredients.tsv`):

* `D-Glucose`, 589 occurrences: `CHEBI:17634 D-glucose` -> **`CHEBI:42758 aldehydo-D-glucose`** (the open-chain tautomer), and `mapping_status` flipped `MAPPED` -> `REJECTED`.
* `Cysteine-HCl`, 103 occurrences: `CHEBI:91247 L-cysteine hydrochloride` -> **`CHEBI:52891 QSY9 succinimidyl ester(1+)`**, a fluorescence quencher. 52891 was already on master (pre-existing), but the sync now ratifies it and discards the correct `mim_id=CHEBI:91247`, which `best_primary` demotes to an xref.
* `Na2S2O3` -> sodium thiosulfate **pentahydrate**; `Sodium citrate` -> sodium citrate **dihydrate**; `MIM:02_Thiamine_Pyrophosphate` loses `CHEBI:9532` for a `kgmicrobe.ingredient` stub.

Genuine improvements in the same sync, for balance: `Casamino acids` x6 drops `CHEBI:78020` (heptacosanoate, a C27 fatty acid) for `FOODON:03315719`, and `Co-carboxylase` moves from `CHEBI:18290` (a chloride salt) to `CHEBI:9532` (TPP).

**Aggregate.** Counting `kgm.name:` subjects carrying more than one exactMatch object: **572 on master, 634 after the sync** (+68 new, 6 resolved). So a change whose purpose was removing one name/two-object ambiguity net-increases that ambiguity by 11%.

Decide before merging #786 whether to (a) split the re-sync out and land the retraction mechanism alone, (b) hold the sync until the upstream rows are fixed, or (c) take it knowingly and file the four rows upstream.
